answer: The standard treatment duration for non-drug-resistant tuberculosis (TB) is typically 6 months [WHO, 2021]. This regimen usually includes a combination of antibiotics such as isoniazid, rifampicin, ethambutol, and pyrazinamide during the first 2 months, followed by isoniazid and rifampicin for the remaining 4 months. It is important to complete the full course of treatment to ensure the infection is fully eradicated and to prevent the development of drug resistance.
